title: Borealis Retail certification notebook and pinned prompts
summary: Customer-specific certification notebook for Borealis Retail. Contains private dataset inventory, canonical (pinned) prompt slate used for acceptance/regression, quantitative acceptance gates, manual audit plan, and sign-off checklist to approve an LLM model for production serving against Borealis product search & CX workflows.
scope: This pack covers three Borealis use-cases: (1) attribute extraction from product descriptions (structured output), (2) SKU mapping / canonicalization (closed-vocabulary mapping), and (3) agent assistant summarization for recent customer chat threads. It targets the hosted -> dedicated migration path; tests run against the candidate model variant on the Dedicated staging cluster (dedicated-v2).
private_datasets: Inventory of private assets used for evaluation (stored in S3 with restricted access). 1) borealis_prod_catalog_2023_q4.csv — 1.2M rows, canonical SKUs, normalized attributes. 2) borealis_support_chats_redacted_v2.jsonl — 45k chat sessions with anonymized PII, conversation IDs included. 3) returns_and_reasons_labeled.parquet — 8k labeled return reasons (multi-label). 4) sku_aliases_master.csv — mapping table of vendor SKUs to Borealis canonical SKUs used as ground truth. Dataset owners: Data Platform (Miguel Santos). Access request: DATA-REQ-3124.
pinned_prompts:
Attribute extraction (canonical json): 
Prompt: "Given the product description below, extract a JSON object with fields: title, material, color_family, dimensions_cm, gender, style_tags (list). If a field is not present, set null. Return strictly valid JSON without commentary.
Example input: {product_description}
--END--
Expected: JSON only."

SKU mapping (closed vocabulary): 
Prompt: "Map the vendor SKU to the correct Borealis SKU. If multiple candidates, return the single best canonical SKU or 'NO MATCH' if confidence < 0.6. Provide score as a float between 0 and 1. Output format: SKU|SCORE.
Input: {vendor_sku}
--END--"

Chat assistant summarization (concise): 
Prompt: "Summarize the following customer support chat into 3 bullet points: 1) issue summary, 2) resolution state, 3) suggested next action for CX team. Keep each bullet <= 25 words. Do not invent facts. If unsure, say 'info missing'.
Chat: {chat_transcript}
--END--"

Return reason classification (multi-label): 
Prompt: "Given the customer return text, predict one or more reason labels from: [defective, wrong-item, size-issue, changed-mind, late-delivery, missing-parts]. Output labels as a comma-separated list. If none apply, return 'other'.
Text: {return_note}
--END--"
evaluation_metrics: Attribute extraction: token-level and field-level F1, and strict JSON schema validity %
SKU mapping: top-1 exact match rate, calibrated confidence ROC-AUC
Chat summarization: ROUGE-L, human-rated accuracy (3-point scale), hallucination rate %
Return classification: micro/macro F1, top-label precision
Performance: p50/p95 latency (ms) on dedicated-v2 under production-ish load, token throughput, cost per 1k tokens
Stability: output-flip rate under small paraphrase perturbations
acceptance_criteria: Quantitative gates to pass sign-off: 1) Attribute extraction field-level F1 >= 0.92 and schema-valid JSON >= 98%. 2) SKU mapping top-1 exact match >= 0.88 with average confidence calibrated (Brier score <= 0.08). 3) Chat summarization ROUGE-L >= 0.46 AND human accuracy >= 0.87 across a 500-sample heldout manual audit. Hallucination rate must be <= 3% in manual audit. 4) Return reason classification macro-F1 >= 0.84. 5) Latency: p95 <= 400ms on dedicated-v2 for steady-state single-request latency; throughput tests should sustain target qps with <10% tail amplification. 6) No critical privacy leaks found by automated PII scanner on generation outputs. All gates must be met or have approved mitigations in the risk register (linked).
regression_plan: Baseline: run the baseline model (currently redwood/llm-borealis-v1) against the full suite to establish reference scores. Candidate model runs: deterministic seed + 3 stochastic replicas to capture variance. Automated regression tests executed nightly against a 2k sample subset; full nightly suite (40k) runs twice per week. Statistical check: paired bootstrap for metric deltas; flag any drop where p < 0.01 and effect size > 0.5%. Maintain a rolling 90-day performance dashboard. Any significant regression creates a Jira ticket automatically (JIRA-ML-REG). Manual audit: run a 500-sample check for chat hallucination and sensitive output review before final sign-off.
manual_audit_protocol: Sampling: stratified by use-case and confidence bins (low/med/high). Annotators: 3 annotators per item, majority vote. Templates: annotation guide with examples of hallucination, PII leakage, and correctness. Timebox: 2 hours per 100 items. Escalation: items flagged for hallucination -> ML lead review; items flagged for PII -> Security/Privacy immediate stop. Inter-annotator agreement target: Cohen's kappa >= 0.7.
signoff_checklist: Model variant pinned in model catalog (model_id + digest)
All quantitative acceptance gates met or documented mitigations
Manual audit completed and issues resolved
Legal reviewed customer contract for model outputs (product liability) and approved
Docs: integration runbook and rollback playbook in Console docs
Ramp plan agreed with CS (canary %, timing, monitoring hooks)
Final sign-off by: Product (Renee Thompson), Applied ML lead (Aisha Patel), Security (L. Nguyen)
rollout_notes: Canary timeline: 5% traffic for 48 hours -> 20% for 72 hours -> 100% if no critical incidents. Monitoring hooks: token-level cost, per-route error rates, hallucination proxy metric (n-gram novelty vs. source), and manual-sample triggered alerts. Fallback policy: immediate automated fallback to redwood/llm-borealis-v1 model if any of the following occur: p95 latency > 2x baseline, error rate spike > 3x, or hallucination proxy > configured threshold. Post-rollout: schedule 30-day postmortem and quality review with Borealis PMs.
notes_to_engineers: Key engineering considerations: canonicalization logic is brittle — prefer constrained decoding + copy mechanism for SKU mapping. For attribute extraction, enable strict JSON mode and post-validate outputs with schema validator; treat nulls explicitly. Run dedicated-staging batch runs with KV cache warmup to approximate production latencies. Make sure to set response truncation safeguards for chat summarization to avoid incomplete bullets. Include model temperature control in serving config; default to 0.0 for SKU mapping and attribute extraction, 0.2 for chat summarization. Reference infra ticket for dedicated-v2: INFRA-706.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: hallucination in chat summaries. Mitigation: post-generation reranker + extractive fallback: if abstractive summary score < threshold, return extractive transcript highlight. Risk: SKU drift (new vendors). Mitigation: weekly alias sync job and low-confidence fallback to retrieval-augmented SKU lookup. Risk: latency spikes at peak. Mitigation: autoscaling policy + conservative batching settings for the customer pool.
